ko.title: [소매 101 #6] 주머니 속의 진열대: 매장 없는 소매

segments.src: > Non-store retailing doesn't delete the costs of a store — it trades rent and shelf space for shipping, returns, and the price of getting your attention.
segments.tr: > 무점포 소매는 매장의 비용을 없애지 않습니다 — 임차료와 진열 공간을 배송, 반품, 그리고 고객의 관심을 끌기 위한 비용으로 교환할 뿐입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Every lecture so far has assumed a building: a sales floor, a door, a trade area of people who live close enough to walk in.
segments.tr: 지금까지의 모든 강의는 건물을 전제했습니다: 판매 공간, 입구, 그리고 걸어서 올 수 있을 정도로 가깝게 사는 사람들의 상권입니다.

segments.src: **Non-store retailing** is everything that sells to final consumers without that floor — direct selling (the Mary Kay rep), automated vending (the machine in the hotel lobby), catalogs and direct mail, TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce.
segments.tr: **무점포 소매**는 그 판매 공간 없이 최종 소비자에게 판매하는 모든 것입니다 — 직접 판매(메리 케이 담당자), 자동 판매(호텔 로비의 기계), 카탈로그와 직접 우편, TV 홈쇼핑, 온라인 마켓플레이스, 그리고 모바일 커머스입니다.

segments.src: The three that matter most today are the last three.
segments.tr: 오늘날 가장 중요한 세 가지는 마지막 세 가지입니다.

segments.src: Here's the useful way to think about them.
segments.tr: 이것들을 생각하는 유용한 방법이 있습니다.

segments.src: A physical store operates under three hard limits:
segments.tr: 물리적 매장은 세 가지 엄격한 제한 하에서 작동합니다:

segments.src: 1. **Shelf space** — a Target carries maybe 80,000 items because that's what fits.
segments.tr: 1. **진열 공간** — Target은 약 80,000개 상품을 취급합니다. 그것이 맞기 때문입니다.

segments.src: 2. **Store hours** — closed at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 2. **영업 시간** — 오후 11시에 문을 닫습니다.

segments.src: 3. **Trade area** — it sells to whoever is within a reasonable drive.
segments.tr: 3. **상권** — 합리적인 거리 내에 있는 누구에게나 판매합니다.

segments.src: Non-store formats break all three.
segments.tr: 무점포 형식은 이 세 가지를 모두 깹니다.

segments.src: An online marketplace has an *endless aisle*: adding the 400,000th product costs a database row, not a square foot.
segments.tr: 온라인 마켓플레이스는 *무한 진열대*를 가집니다: 400,000번째 상품을 추가하는 데는 데이터베이스 행의 비용이 들지, 평방피트의 비용이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's open at 2 a.m.
segments.tr: 오전 2시에도 열어있습니다.

segments.src: Its trade area is the shipping map.
segments.tr: 그 상권은 배송 지도입니다.

segments.src: But — and this is the part beginners miss — **you don't escape cost, you swap it.** A store's big costs are rent, store labor, and inventory sitting on shelves.
segments.tr: 하지만 — 이것이 초보자들이 놓치는 부분입니다 — **비용을 피하는 게 아니라 교환할 뿐입니다.** 매장의 큰 비용은 임차료, 점원 인건비, 그리고 진열대에 앉아있는 재고입니다.

segments.src: A non-store retailer pays little rent, and instead pays for:
segments.tr: 무점포 소매업체는 임차료를 거의 내지 않지만, 대신 다음에 대해 비용을 지급합니다:

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition** — a store on a busy corner gets foot traffic for free. An online seller buys every visitor through ads, search placement, or a marketplace commission.
segments.tr: - **고객 획득** — 번화한 모퉁이의 매장은 발길이 무료로 들어옵니다. 온라인 판매자는 광고, 검색 순위, 또는 마켓플레이스 수수료를 통해 모든 방문자를 구매합니다.

segments.src: - **Fulfillment and the last mile** — picking, packing, and driving one box to one doorstep. A store makes the *customer* do that leg for free.
segments.tr: - **이행 및 마지막 마일** — 한 상자를 픽업하고 포장한 후 한 집 입구까지 배송합니다. 매장은 *고객*에게 그 구간을 무료로 하도록 합니다.

segments.src: - **Returns (reverse logistics)** — a shopper who can't touch the product buys two sizes and sends one back. Online return rates run well above in-store rates, and apparel is the worst offender. Each return means shipping paid twice, inspection, repackaging, and often a markdown.
segments.tr: - **반품(역물류)** — 상품을 만져볼 수 없는 쇼퍼는 두 사이즈를 사서 하나를 반품합니다. 온라인 반품률은 매장 내 반품률보다 훨씬 높으며, 의류가 가장 심합니다. 각 반품은 배송비를 두 번 내고, 검사하고, 재포장하고, 종종 가격을 인하하는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: And because the shopper can't touch anything, the retailer must supply **trust substitutes**: photos and video, ratings and reviews, size charts, a generous return policy, a recognizable brand.
segments.tr: 그리고 쇼퍼가 아무것도 만져볼 수 없기 때문에, 소매업체는 **신뢰 대체품**을 제공해야 합니다: 사진과 비디오, 평점과 리뷰, 사이즈 차트, 관대한 반품 정책, 인식할 수 있는 브랜드.

segments.src: That's not marketing decoration.
segments.tr: 그것은 마케팅 장식이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's doing the job the shelf used to do.
segments.tr: 그것은 진열대가 예전에 하던 일을 하는 것입니다.

segments.src: One more distinction worth carrying around — **who controls the clock**:
segments.tr: 기억해 둘 만한 또 다른 구분이 있습니다 — **누가 시간을 통제하는가**:

segments.src: - **TV home shopping** — the *seller* controls it. A scheduled hour, a host demonstrating, a countdown, "only 300 left." You didn't go looking; the format created the demand.
segments.tr: - **TV 홈쇼핑** — *판매자*가 통제합니다. 정해진 시간, 진행자의 시연, 카운트다운, "남은 것 300개뿐입니다." 당신이 찾아간 게 아닙니다; 형식이 수요를 만들었습니다.

segments.src: - **Online marketplace** — the *shopper* controls it. You search, filter, compare, and buy on your own schedule. Demand already existed; the retailer competes on price, selection, and delivery speed.
segments.tr: - **온라인 마켓플레이스** — *쇼퍼*가 통제합니다. 당신은 검색하고, 필터링하고, 비교하고, 자신의 일정에 맞춰 구매합니다. 수요는 이미 존재했습니다; 소매업체는 가격, 선택, 그리고 배송 속도로 경쟁합니다.

segments.src: - **Mobile / social commerce** — back to the seller. A feed pushes you something you weren't shopping for, and checkout takes fifteen seconds because your card is already saved.
segments.tr: - **모바일/소셜 커머스** — 판매자에게 돌아갑니다. 피드가 당신이 쇼핑하지 않던 것을 밀어붙이고, 카드가 이미 저장되어 있어서 결제가 15초 만에 끝납니다.

segments.src: Which is why **live commerce** — a host demonstrating a product in a live stream with a countdown — isn't new at all.
segments.tr: 따라서 **라이브 커머스** — 진행자가 라이브 스트림에서 카운트다운으로 상품을 시연하는 — 전혀 새로운 것이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's TV home shopping, rebuilt on a phone, with a comment section.
segments.tr: 그것은 TV 홈쇼핑을 휴대폰에 재구성하고 댓글 섹션을 추가한 것입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활에서

segments.src: It's Sunday, 9 p.m., and you're on the couch in Columbus.
segments.tr: 일요일 오후 9시, 당신은 콜럼버스의 소파에 앉아있습니다.

segments.src: You land on QVC.
segments.tr: 당신은 QVC에 접속합니다.

segments.src: A host is demonstrating a countertop grill — flipping it open, pressing a sandwich, talking about the removable plates.
segments.tr: 진행자가 조리대용 그릴을 시연하고 있습니다 — 덮개를 열고, 샌드위치를 누르고, 분리 가능한 판에 대해 설명합니다.

segments.src: A counter on screen says how many have sold, and the price is only good for this segment.
segments.tr: 화면의 카운터는 얼마나 많은 상품이 팔렸는지 보여주고, 가격은 이 세그먼트에만 유효합니다.

segments.src: You weren't shopping for a grill.
segments.tr: 당신은 그릴을 쇼핑하고 있지 않았습니다.

segments.src: That's the point: **seller-controlled time, demonstration, urgency.** Home shopping has thrived for decades on categories that are hard to judge from a photo but easy to *show* — kitchen gadgets, jewelry, skincare, mattresses.
segments.tr: 그것이 포인트입니다: **판매자 통제 시간, 시연, 긴박감.** 홈쇼핑은 사진으로는 판단하기 어렵지만 *보여주기*는 쉬운 카테고리에서 수십 년 동안 번창했습니다 — 주방 용품, 보석, 스킨케어, 매트리스.

segments.src: You pick up your phone instead and search Amazon for "panini press."
segments.tr: 대신 핸드폰을 들고 Amazon에서 "파니니 프레스"를 검색합니다.

segments.src: Forty results, sorted by review count.
segments.tr: 리뷰 수로 정렬된 40개의 결과가 있습니다.

segments.src: You read three one-star reviews, check that it's Prime, and see it arrives Tuesday.
segments.tr: 당신은 1별 리뷰 3개를 읽고, Prime 상태를 확인하고, 화요일에 도착함을 봅니다.

segments.src: **Shopper-controlled time.** Nobody persuaded you of anything; you compared and picked.
segments.tr: **쇼퍼 통제 시간.** 아무도 당신을 설득하지 않았습니다; 당신이 비교하고 선택했습니다.

segments.src: Then you open Instagram and a video shows leggings for $34.
segments.tr: 그러면 당신은 Instagram을 열고 $34에 레깅스를 보여주는 비디오를 봅니다.

segments.src: Two taps, Apple Pay, done, before the video finishes.
segments.tr: 두 번 탭, Apple Pay, 완료, 비디오가 끝나기 전에.

segments.src: You never visited a website.
segments.tr: 당신은 웹사이트를 방문한 적이 없습니다.

segments.src: In the U.S., most e-commerce traffic now comes through a phone, and checkout friction — not price — is often what decides the sale.
segments.tr: 미국에서는 대부분의 전자상거래 트래픽이 이제 휴대폰을 통해 발생하며, 결제 마찰 — 가격이 아니라 — 판매를 결정하는 것이 종종입니다.

segments.src: Three retail formats, one couch, twenty minutes.
segments.tr: 세 가지 소매 형식, 한 개의 소파, 20분.

segments.src: Now the economics.
segments.tr: 이제 경제학입니다.

segments.src: The leggings don't fit.
segments.tr: 레깅스가 맞지 않습니다.

segments.src: You get a free return label, drop the bag at the UPS counter inside a Kohl's, and forget about it.
segments.tr: 무료 반품 레이블을 받고, Kohl's 내부의 UPS 카운터에 가방을 떨어뜨린 후 잊어버립니다.

segments.src: For you it cost nothing.
segments.tr: 당신에게는 비용이 들지 않습니다.

segments.src: For the seller: outbound shipping, return shipping, someone inspecting the bag, and possibly reselling at a discount.
segments.tr: 판매자에게: 아웃바운드 배송, 반품 배송, 누군가 가방을 검사, 그리고 아마도 할인 가격으로 재판매.

segments.src: That single return can erase the margin on the sale — which is exactly why "free returns" is quietly disappearing at a lot of retailers, and why buy-online-pickup-in-store exists.
segments.tr: 그 하나의 반품은 판매 마진을 지울 수 있습니다 — 이것이 정확히 "무료 반품"이 많은 소매업체에서 조용히 사라지고 있는 이유이며, "온라인 구매 매장 픽업"이 존재하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: BOPIS lets the store's building do the last mile for free.
segments.tr: BOPIS는 매장의 건물이 마지막 마일을 무료로 하도록 합니다.

segments.src: And a number worth keeping in your head: e-commerce is roughly **one in six** U.S.
segments.tr: 그리고 기억해 둘 만한 숫자: 전자상거래는 대략 **6명 중 1명**입니다. U.S.

segments.src: retail dollars, per Census Bureau estimates.
segments.tr: 소매 달러, 인구조사국 추정에 따르면.

segments.src: Enormous — and also a reminder that about five in six are still spent in a building.
segments.tr: 엄청나다 — 그리고 약 6명 중 5명은 여전히 건물에서 지출된다는 것을 상기시켜줍니다.

segments.src: Non-store retailing didn't replace stores.
segments.tr: 무점포 소매는 매장을 대체하지 않았습니다.

segments.src: It stripped them of their monopoly on selection, hours, and geography, and forced them to compete on the things a warehouse can't do.
segments.tr: 그것은 그들로부터 선택, 시간, 그리고 지리의 독점권을 빼앗았고, 창고가 할 수 없는 것들에서 경쟁하도록 강요했습니다.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Non-store retailing sells without a sales floor — TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce are its dominant modern forms.
segments.tr: 1. 무점포 소매는 판매 공간 없이 판매합니다 — TV 홈쇼핑, 온라인 마켓플레이스, 그리고 모바일 커머스는 그 주요 현대 형식입니다.

segments.src: 2. It escapes rent, shelf limits, store hours, and trade-area boundaries, but pays for it in customer acquisition, last-mile delivery, and returns.
segments.tr: 2. 그것은 임차료, 진열 한계, 영업 시간, 그리고 상권 경계를 벗어나지만, 고객 획득, 마지막 마일 배송, 그리고 반품으로 대가를 치룹니다.

segments.src: 3. The formats differ by *who controls the clock*: home shopping and social feeds create demand; search-driven marketplaces capture demand that already exists.
segments.tr: 3. 형식은 *누가 시간을 통제하는가*에 따라 다릅니다: 홈쇼핑과 소셜 피드는 수요를 만들고; 검색 기반 마켓플레이스는 이미 존재하는 수요를 포착합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자기 평가

segments.src: **1.** Which cost is generally *higher* for a pure online retailer than for a comparable physical store?
segments.tr: **1.** 순수 온라인 소매업체가 비슷한 물리적 매장보다 일반적으로 어느 비용이 *더 높습니까*?

segments.src: - (a) Rent per square foot
segments.tr: - (a) 평방피트당 임차료

segments.src: - (b) In-store labor
segments.tr: - (b) 매장 내 노동

segments.src: - (c) Reverse logistics (handling returns)
segments.tr: - (c) 역물류(반품 처리)

segments.src: - (d) Shrinkage from shoplifting
segments.tr: - (d) 소매치기로 인한 손실

segments.src: **2.** TV home shopping and live-stream commerce share the same core mechanic: the seller controls when the product is shown and creates urgency around it.
segments.tr: **2.** TV 홈쇼핑과 라이브 스트림 커머스는 동일한 핵심 메커니즘을 공유합니다: 판매자가 상품을 보여주는 시간을 통제하고 그 주변에 긴급성을 만듭니다.

segments.src: **3.** "Endless aisle" refers to:
segments.tr: **3.** "무한 진열대"는 다음을 의미합니다:

segments.src: - (a) A warehouse club's long shelving runs
segments.tr: - (a) 창고 클럽의 긴 진열 행들

segments.src: - (b) An online retailer's ability to list far more SKUs than a store can stock
segments.tr: - (b) 온라인 소매업체가 매장이 재고할 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 많은 SKU를 나열할 수 있는 능력

segments.src: - (c) A store layout that forces shoppers past every category
segments.tr: - (c) 모든 카테고리를 지나가도록 쇼퍼를 강제하는 매장 레이아웃

segments.src: - (d) A 24-hour store format
segments.tr: - (d) 24시간 매장 형식

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Non-store retailing** — selling to final consumers without a fixed physical sales floor: direct selling, vending, catalogs, TV home shopping, e-commerce, and m-commerce.
segments.tr: - **무점포 소매** — 고정된 물리적 판매 공간 없이 최종 소비자에게 판매: 직접 판매, 판매, 카탈로그, TV 홈쇼핑, 전자상거래, 및 모바일 커머스.

segments.src: - **Endless aisle** — the ability to offer a near-unlimited assortment because listings cost data storage rather than shelf space.
segments.tr: - **무한 진열대** — 나열이 진열 공간이 아니라 데이터 저장소의 비용이 들기 때문에 거의 무제한적인 분류를 제공할 수 있는 능력.

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition cost (CAC)** — what a retailer pays in ads, commissions, or promotions to bring in one buying customer; the online substitute for a good street corner.
segments.tr: - **고객 획득 비용(CAC)** — 소매업체가 한 명의 구매 고객을 끌어오기 위해 광고, 수수료, 또는 프로모션으로 지불하는 것; 좋은 모퉁이의 온라인 대체물.

segments.src: - **Last mile** — the final delivery leg from local facility to the customer's door; the most expensive stretch of the supply chain, and the one stores hand to the shopper for free.
segments.tr: - **마지막 마일** — 지역 시설에서 고객의 집 입구까지의 최종 배송 구간; 공급 체인에서 가장 비용이 많이 드는 구간, 그리고 매장이 쇼퍼에게 무료로 넘기는 것.

segments.src: - **Reverse logistics** — the process and cost of moving returned goods back, inspecting, restocking, or disposing of them.

zh.title: [零售基础 101 #6] 口袋里的货架：无店铺零售

segments.src: > Non-store retailing doesn't delete the costs of a store — it trades rent and shelf space for shipping, returns, and the price of getting your attention.
segments.tr: > 无店铺零售并不是消除了商店的成本——而是把租赁费和货架空间换成了运费、退货费和获取你的注意力的代价。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Every lecture so far has assumed a building: a sales floor, a door, a trade area of people who live close enough to walk in.
segments.tr: 到目前为止，每场讲座都假设了一座建筑的存在：一个销售楼层、一扇门、一个由足够靠近以至于可以步行进来的人群构成的交易区域。

segments.src: **Non-store retailing** is everything that sells to final consumers without that floor — direct selling (the Mary Kay rep), automated vending (the machine in the hotel lobby), catalogs and direct mail, TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce.
segments.tr: **无店铺零售**是指所有不通过销售楼层就能向最终消费者销售的方式——直接销售（玛丽凯代表）、自动售货（酒店大堂的机器）、目录和直邮、电视家庭购物、在线市场和移动商务。

segments.src: The three that matter most today are the last three.
segments.tr: 今天最重要的三种是最后这三种。

segments.src: Here's the useful way to think about them.
segments.tr: 这是思考它们的有用方式。

segments.src: A physical store operates under three hard limits:
segments.tr: 实体店在三个硬性限制下运营：

segments.src: 1. **Shelf space** — a Target carries maybe 80,000 items because that's what fits.
segments.tr: 1. **货架空间** — 目标百货大约有80,000件商品，因为那是能放下的量。

segments.src: 2. **Store hours** — closed at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 2. **营业时间** — 晚上11点关闭。

segments.src: 3. **Trade area** — it sells to whoever is within a reasonable drive.
segments.tr: 3. **交易区域** — 它只向在合理车程范围内的人销售。

segments.src: Non-store formats break all three.
segments.tr: 无店铺格式打破了这三个限制。

segments.src: An online marketplace has an *endless aisle*: adding the 400,000th product costs a database row, not a square foot.
segments.tr: 在线市场有一个*无限货架*：添加第400,000件产品只需花费一行数据库记录，而不是一平方英尺。

segments.src: It's open at 2 a.m.
segments.tr: 它在凌晨2点开放。

segments.src: Its trade area is the shipping map.
segments.tr: 它的交易区域就是运输地图。

segments.src: But — and this is the part beginners miss — **you don't escape cost, you swap it.** A store's big costs are rent, store labor, and inventory sitting on shelves.
segments.tr: 但是——这是初学者容易忽视的部分——**你并不能逃脱成本，你只是转换了它。** 商店的主要成本是租赁费、店铺劳动力和货架上堆积的库存。

segments.src: A non-store retailer pays little rent, and instead pays for:
segments.tr: 无店铺零售商支付的租赁费很少，但要支付：

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition** — a store on a busy corner gets foot traffic for free. An online seller buys every visitor through ads, search placement, or a marketplace commission.
segments.tr: - **客户获取** — 位于繁华角落的商店免费获得人流量。在线卖家通过广告、搜索排名或市场佣金来购买每个访客。

segments.src: - **Fulfillment and the last mile** — picking, packing, and driving one box to one doorstep. A store makes the *customer* do that leg for free.
segments.tr: - **履行和最后一英里** — 拣选、打包和运送一个盒子到一个门步。商店让*客户*免费完成这一段。

segments.src: - **Returns (reverse logistics)** — a shopper who can't touch the product buys two sizes and sends one back. Online return rates run well above in-store rates, and apparel is the worst offender. Each return means shipping paid twice, inspection, repackaging, and often a markdown.
segments.tr: - **退货（逆向物流）** — 无法接触产品的购物者购买两种尺寸并退回一种。在线退货率远高于店内退货率，服装是最严重的违规者。每次退货都意味着运费支付两次、检查、重新包装，通常还有降价。

segments.src: And because the shopper can't touch anything, the retailer must supply **trust substitutes**: photos and video, ratings and reviews, size charts, a generous return policy, a recognizable brand.
segments.tr: 由于购物者无法接触任何东西，零售商必须提供**信任替代品**：照片和视频、评分和评论、尺码表、慷慨的退货政策、知名品牌。

segments.src: That's not marketing decoration.
segments.tr: 这不是营销装饰。

segments.src: It's doing the job the shelf used to do.
segments.tr: 这是在做货架曾经做的工作。

segments.src: One more distinction worth carrying around — **who controls the clock**:
segments.tr: 还有一个值得记住的区别——**谁控制时间**：

segments.src: - **TV home shopping** — the *seller* controls it. A scheduled hour, a host demonstrating, a countdown, "only 300 left." You didn't go looking; the format created the demand.
segments.tr: - **电视家庭购物** — *卖家*控制它。一个计划时间、一个主持人演示、一个倒计时、"只剩300个"。你没有主动寻找；这个格式创造了需求。

segments.src: - **Online marketplace** — the *shopper* controls it. You search, filter, compare, and buy on your own schedule. Demand already existed; the retailer competes on price, selection, and delivery speed.
segments.tr: - **在线市场** — *购物者*控制它。你按自己的日程搜索、筛选、比较和购买。需求已经存在；零售商在价格、选择和交付速度上竞争。

segments.src: - **Mobile / social commerce** — back to the seller. A feed pushes you something you weren't shopping for, and checkout takes fifteen seconds because your card is already saved.
segments.tr: - **移动/社交商务** — 回到卖家。一个动态推送你本不打算购物的东西，结账只需15秒，因为你的卡已保存。

segments.src: Which is why **live commerce** — a host demonstrating a product in a live stream with a countdown — isn't new at all.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么**直播商务**——一个主持人在直播中演示产品并设置倒计时——一点也不新鲜。

segments.src: It's TV home shopping, rebuilt on a phone, with a comment section.
segments.tr: 这是电视家庭购物，在手机上重建，增加了评论区。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: It's Sunday, 9 p.m., and you're on the couch in Columbus.
segments.tr: 这是星期日晚上9点，你坐在哥伦布的沙发上。

segments.src: You land on QVC.
segments.tr: 你登陆了QVC。

segments.src: A host is demonstrating a countertop grill — flipping it open, pressing a sandwich, talking about the removable plates.
segments.tr: 一位主持人正在演示一台台面烤架——翻打开它、压制一个三明治、谈论可拆卸的盘子。

segments.src: A counter on screen says how many have sold, and the price is only good for this segment.
segments.tr: 屏幕上的计数器显示已售出多少个，价格仅对本时段有效。

segments.src: You weren't shopping for a grill.
segments.tr: 你本来不是在买烤架。

segments.src: That's the point: **seller-controlled time, demonstration, urgency.** Home shopping has thrived for decades on categories that are hard to judge from a photo but easy to *show* — kitchen gadgets, jewelry, skincare, mattresses.
segments.tr: 这正是重点：**卖家控制的时间、演示、紧迫感。** 家庭购物在几十年来在那些难以从照片判断但易于*展示*的类别上蓬勃发展——厨房小工具、珠宝、护肤品、床垫。

segments.src: You pick up your phone instead and search Amazon for "panini press."
segments.tr: 你改为拿起手机，在亚马逊上搜索"帕尼尼压榨机"。

segments.src: Forty results, sorted by review count.
segments.tr: 40个结果，按评论数排序。

segments.src: You read three one-star reviews, check that it's Prime, and see it arrives Tuesday.
segments.tr: 你阅读了三条一星评论，检查它是否为Prime，并看到它在星期二到达。

segments.src: **Shopper-controlled time.** Nobody persuaded you of anything; you compared and picked.
segments.tr: **购物者控制的时间。** 没有人说服你任何东西；你自己比较并选择了。

segments.src: Then you open Instagram and a video shows leggings for $34.
segments.tr: 然后你打开Instagram，一个视频展示了价格为$34的打底裤。

segments.src: Two taps, Apple Pay, done, before the video finishes.
segments.tr: 两下点击，Apple Pay，完成，在视频结束之前。

segments.src: You never visited a website.
segments.tr: 你从未访问过网站。

segments.src: In the U.S., most e-commerce traffic now comes through a phone, and checkout friction — not price — is often what decides the sale.
segments.tr: 在美国，大多数电子商务流量现在通过手机进行，结账摩擦——而不是价格——通常是决定销售的因素。

segments.src: Three retail formats, one couch, twenty minutes.
segments.tr: 三种零售格式，一个沙发，二十分钟。

segments.src: Now the economics.
segments.tr: 现在说经济学。

segments.src: The leggings don't fit.
segments.tr: 打底裤不合身。

segments.src: You get a free return label, drop the bag at the UPS counter inside a Kohl's, and forget about it.
segments.tr: 你得到一个免费退货标签，在科尔百货内的UPS柜台放下包包，忘掉它。

segments.src: For you it cost nothing.
segments.tr: 对你来说没有成本。

segments.src: For the seller: outbound shipping, return shipping, someone inspecting the bag, and possibly reselling at a discount.
segments.tr: 对于卖家：出站运费、退货运费、有人检查包包，可能以折扣价重新出售。

segments.src: That single return can erase the margin on the sale — which is exactly why "free returns" is quietly disappearing at a lot of retailers, and why buy-online-pickup-in-store exists.
segments.tr: 那一次退货可以抹掉销售利润——这正是为什么"免费退货"在许多零售商中悄悄消失，以及为什么存在"在线购买店内取货"的原因。

segments.src: BOPIS lets the store's building do the last mile for free.
segments.tr: BOPIS让商店的建筑免费完成最后一英里。

segments.src: And a number worth keeping in your head: e-commerce is roughly **one in six** U.S.
segments.tr: 还有一个值得记住的数字：电子商务大约占美国**六分之一**。

segments.src: retail dollars, per Census Bureau estimates.
segments.tr: 零售美元，根据人口普查局的估计。

segments.src: Enormous — and also a reminder that about five in six are still spent in a building.
segments.tr: 巨大——也提醒我们大约六分之五仍然在建筑内花费。

segments.src: Non-store retailing didn't replace stores.
segments.tr: 无店铺零售并没有替代商店。

segments.src: It stripped them of their monopoly on selection, hours, and geography, and forced them to compete on the things a warehouse can't do.
segments.tr: 它剥夺了它们在选择、时间和地理位置上的垄断，迫使它们在仓库做不到的事情上竞争。

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Non-store retailing sells without a sales floor — TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce are its dominant modern forms.
segments.tr: 1. 无店铺零售不需要销售楼层就能销售——电视家庭购物、在线市场和移动商务是其主要的现代形式。

segments.src: 2. It escapes rent, shelf limits, store hours, and trade-area boundaries, but pays for it in customer acquisition, last-mile delivery, and returns.
segments.tr: 2. 它逃脱了租赁、货架限制、营业时间和交易区域界限，但要为客户获取、最后一英里交付和退货付出代价。

segments.src: 3. The formats differ by *who controls the clock*: home shopping and social feeds create demand; search-driven marketplaces capture demand that already exists.
segments.tr: 3. 这些格式在*谁控制时间*上有所不同：家庭购物和社交动态创造需求；搜索驱动的市场捕获已经存在的需求。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.src: **1.** Which cost is generally *higher* for a pure online retailer than for a comparable physical store?
segments.tr: **1.** 与相比的实体店相比，纯在线零售商的哪项成本通常*更高*？

segments.src: - (a) Rent per square foot
segments.tr: - (a) 每平方英尺的租赁费

segments.src: - (b) In-store labor
segments.tr: - (b) 店内劳动力

segments.src: - (c) Reverse logistics (handling returns)
segments.tr: - (c) 逆向物流（处理退货）

segments.src: - (d) Shrinkage from shoplifting
segments.tr: - (d) 盗窃导致的缩水

segments.src: **2.** TV home shopping and live-stream commerce share the same core mechanic: the seller controls when the product is shown and creates urgency around it.
segments.tr: **2.** 电视家庭购物和直播商务共享相同的核心机制：卖家控制产品何时展示并围绕它创造紧迫感。

segments.src: **3.** "Endless aisle" refers to:
segments.tr: **3.** "无限货架"指的是：

segments.src: - (a) A warehouse club's long shelving runs
segments.tr: - (a) 仓库俱乐部的长货架排

segments.src: - (b) An online retailer's ability to list far more SKUs than a store can stock
segments.tr: - (b) 在线零售商能够列出远比商店能库存更多的SKU

segments.src: - (c) A store layout that forces shoppers past every category
segments.tr: - (c) 强制购物者经过每个类别的商店布局

segments.src: - (d) A 24-hour store format
segments.tr: - (d) 24小时商店格式

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Non-store retailing** — selling to final consumers without a fixed physical sales floor: direct selling, vending, catalogs, TV home shopping, e-commerce, and m-commerce.
segments.tr: - **无店铺零售** — 不通过固定的实体销售楼层向最终消费者销售：直接销售、售货、目录、电视家庭购物、电子商务和移动商务。

segments.src: - **Endless aisle** — the ability to offer a near-unlimited assortment because listings cost data storage rather than shelf space.
segments.tr: - **无限货架** — 能够提供几乎无限种类的能力，因为列表成本是数据存储而不是货架空间。

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition cost (CAC)** — what a retailer pays in ads, commissions, or promotions to bring in one buying customer; the online substitute for a good street corner.
segments.tr: - **客户获取成本（CAC）** — 零售商为了吸引一个购买客户在广告、佣金或促销中支付的费用；在线版本的良好街角的替代品。

segments.src: - **Last mile** — the final delivery leg from local facility to the customer's door; the most expensive stretch of the supply chain, and the one stores hand to the shopper for free.
segments.tr: - **最后一英里** — 从本地设施到客户门口的最后交付段；供应链中最昂贵的一段，也是商店免费交给购物者的一段。

segments.src: - **Reverse logistics** — the process and cost of moving returned goods back, inspecting, restocking, or disposing of them.
segments.tr: - **逆向物流** — 返回、检查、重新库存或处理退货商品的流程和成本。

segments.src: - **Live commerce** — real-time video selling with in-stream checkout; structurally, TV home shopping rebuilt for mobile.
segments.tr: - **直播商务** — 带有流内结账的实时视频销售；结构上是为移动设备重建的电视家庭购物。

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — (c).
Without the ability to touch or try the product, online return rates run substantially higher than in-store, especially in apparel, and each return carries shipping, inspection, and markdown costs.
segments.tr: 由于无法接触或尝试产品，在线退货率远高于店内，尤其是服装，每次退货都会产生运费、检查和降价成本。

segments.src: Both are seller-controlled time: a scheduled demonstration plus scarcity cues, which generates demand rather than merely capturing it.
segments.tr: 两者都是卖家控制的时间：计划的演示加上稀缺线索，这产生了需求而不仅仅是捕获它。

segments.src: "Endless aisle" describes assortment freed from physical shelf constraints; the marginal cost of listing another SKU is close to zero.*
segments.tr: "无限货架"描述了不受物理货架限制的分类；列出另一个SKU的边际成本接近零。*

hi.title: [Retailing 101 #6] आपकी जेब में गलियारा: दुकान के बिना खुदरा

segments.src: > Non-store retailing doesn't delete the costs of a store — it trades rent and shelf space for shipping, returns, and the price of getting your attention.
segments.tr: > गैर-दुकान खुदरा एक दुकान की लागत को नहीं हटाता — यह किराया और शेल्फ स्पेस को शिपिंग, रिटर्न और ध्यान आकर्षित करने की कीमत के लिए बदलता है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Every lecture so far has assumed a building: a sales floor, a door, a trade area of people who live close enough to walk in.
segments.tr: अब तक के हर व्याख्यान ने एक इमारत को मान लिया है: एक बिक्री फर्श, एक दरवाजा, लोगों का एक व्यापार क्षेत्र जो चलकर आने के लिए काफी करीब हैं।

segments.src: **Non-store retailing** is everything that sells to final consumers without that floor — direct selling (the Mary Kay rep), automated vending (the machine in the hotel lobby), catalogs and direct mail, TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce.
segments.tr: **गैर-दुकान खुदरा** वह सब कुछ है जो उस फर्श के बिना अंतिम उपभोक्ताओं को बेचता है — प्रत्यक्ष विक्रय (Mary Kay प्रतिनिधि), स्वचालित वेंडिंग (होटल लॉबी में मशीन), कैटलॉग और सीधी मेल, टीवी होम शॉपिंग, ऑनलाइन मार्केटप्लेस, और मोबाइल वाणिज्य।

segments.src: The three that matter most today are the last three.
segments.tr: आज सबसे महत्वपूर्ण तीन अंतिम तीन हैं।

segments.src: Here's the useful way to think about them.
segments.tr: यहाँ उनके बारे में सोचने का उपयोगी तरीका है।

segments.src: A physical store operates under three hard limits:
segments.tr: एक भौतिक दुकान तीन कठोर सीमाओं के तहत काम करती है:

segments.src: 1. **Shelf space** — a Target carries maybe 80,000 items because that's what fits.
segments.tr: 1. **शेल्फ स्पेस** — एक Target शायद 80,000 आइटम ले जाती है क्योंकि यही वह है जो फिट होता है।

segments.src: 2. **Store hours** — closed at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 2. **दुकान के घंटे** — रात 11 बजे बंद।

segments.src: 3. **Trade area** — it sells to whoever is within a reasonable drive.
segments.tr: 3. **व्यापार क्षेत्र** — यह उसे बेचता है जो उचित ड्राइव के भीतर है।

segments.src: Non-store formats break all three.
segments.tr: गैर-दुकान प्रारूप सभी तीनों को तोड़ते हैं।

segments.src: An online marketplace has an *endless aisle*: adding the 400,000th product costs a database row, not a square foot.
segments.tr: एक ऑनलाइन मार्केटप्लेस के पास एक *अंतहीन गलियारा* है: 400,000वां उत्पाद जोड़ने में एक डेटाबेस पंक्ति की लागत होती है, एक वर्ग फुट नहीं।

segments.src: It's open at 2 a.m.
segments.tr: यह सुबह 2 बजे खुला है।

segments.src: Its trade area is the shipping map.
segments.tr: इसका व्यापार क्षेत्र शिपिंग मानचित्र है।

segments.src: But — and this is the part beginners miss — **you don't escape cost, you swap it.** A store's big costs are rent, store labor, and inventory sitting on shelves.
segments.tr: लेकिन — और यह वह हिस्सा है जो शुरुआती लोग याद करते हैं — **आप लागत से नहीं बचते, आप इसे स्वैप करते हैं।** एक दुकान की बड़ी लागतें किराया, दुकान श्रम, और शेल्फ पर बैठा इनवेंटरी हैं।

segments.src: A non-store retailer pays little rent, and instead pays for:
segments.tr: एक गैर-दुकान खुदरा विक्रेता कम किराया देता है, और इसके बजाय के लिए भुगतान करता है:

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition** — a store on a busy corner gets foot traffic for free. An online seller buys every visitor through ads, search placement, or a marketplace commission.
segments.tr: - **ग्राहक अधिग्रहण** — एक व्यस्त कोने पर एक दुकान को पैदल यातायात मुफ्त में मिलता है। एक ऑनलाइन विक्रेता विज्ञापन, खोज प्लेसमेंट, या मार्केटप्लेस कमीशन के माध्यम से हर आगंतुक को खरीदता है।

segments.src: - **Fulfillment and the last mile** — picking, packing, and driving one box to one doorstep. A store makes the *customer* do that leg for free.
segments.tr: - **पूर्ति और अंतिम मील** — एक बॉक्स को एक दरवाजे तक उठाना, पैक करना, और ड्राइव करना। एक दुकान *ग्राहक* को उस पैर को मुफ्त में करती है।

segments.src: - **Returns (reverse logistics)** — a shopper who can't touch the product buys two sizes and sends one back. Online return rates run well above in-store rates, and apparel is the worst offender. Each return means shipping paid twice, inspection, repackaging, and often a markdown.
segments.tr: - **रिटर्न (रिवर्स लॉजिस्टिक्स)** — एक खरीदार जो उत्पाद को छू नहीं सकता, दो आकार खरीदता है और एक वापस भेजता है। ऑनलाइन रिटर्न दरें इन-स्टोर दरों से अच्छी तरह से ऊपर चलती हैं, और परिधान सबसे बुरा अपराधी है। प्रत्येक रिटर्न का मतलब दो बार शिपिंग का भुगतान, निरीक्षण, पुनः पैकेजिंग, और अक्सर एक मार्कडाउन।

segments.src: And because the shopper can't touch anything, the retailer must supply **trust substitutes**: photos and video, ratings and reviews, size charts, a generous return policy, a recognizable brand.
segments.tr: और क्योंकि खरीदार कुछ भी छू नहीं सकता, खुदरा विक्रेता को **विश्वास विकल्प** की आपूर्ति करनी चाहिए: फोटो और वीडियो, रेटिंग और समीक्षा, आकार चार्ट, एक उदार रिटर्न नीति, एक पहचानने योग्य ब्रांड।

segments.src: That's not marketing decoration.
segments.tr: यह विपणन सजावट नहीं है।

segments.src: It's doing the job the shelf used to do.
segments.tr: यह वह काम कर रहा है जो शेल्फ करता था।

segments.src: One more distinction worth carrying around — **who controls the clock**:
segments.tr: एक और अंतर जो ले जाने के लायक है — **जो घड़ी को नियंत्रित करता है**:

segments.src: - **TV home shopping** — the *seller* controls it. A scheduled hour, a host demonstrating, a countdown, "only 300 left." You didn't go looking; the format created the demand.
segments.tr: - **टीवी होम शॉपिंग** — *विक्रेता* इसे नियंत्रित करता है। एक निर्धारित घंटा, एक मेजबान प्रदर्शन, एक काउंटडाउन, "केवल 300 बचे।" आप खोज रहे नहीं गए; प्रारूप ने मांग बनाई।

segments.src: - **Online marketplace** — the *shopper* controls it. You search, filter, compare, and buy on your own schedule. Demand already existed; the retailer competes on price, selection, and delivery speed.
segments.tr: - **ऑनलाइन मार्केटप्लेस** — *खरीदार* इसे नियंत्रित करता है। आप अपने अनुसूची पर खोज, फ़िल्टर, तुलना, और खरीदते हैं। मांग पहले से मौजूद थी; खुदरा विक्रेता मूल्य, चयन, और डिलीवरी गति पर प्रतिस्पर्धा करता है।

segments.src: - **Mobile / social commerce** — back to the seller. A feed pushes you something you weren't shopping for, and checkout takes fifteen seconds because your card is already saved.
segments.tr: - **मोबाइल / सामाजिक वाणिज्य** — विक्रेता के लिए वापस। एक फ़ीड आपको कुछ ऐसा धकेलता है जो आप खरीद रहे नहीं थे, और चेकआउट पंद्रह सेकंड लेता है क्योंकि आपका कार्ड पहले से सहेजा गया है।

segments.src: Which is why **live commerce** — a host demonstrating a product in a live stream with a countdown — isn't new at all.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि **लाइव वाणिज्य** — एक मेजबान काउंटडाउन के साथ एक लाइव स्ट्रीम में एक उत्पाद प्रदर्शन करता है — बिल्कुल नया नहीं है।

segments.src: It's TV home shopping, rebuilt on a phone, with a comment section.
segments.tr: यह टीवी होम शॉपिंग है, एक फोन पर फिर से बनाया गया, एक टिप्पणी अनुभाग के साथ।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: It's Sunday, 9 p.m., and you're on the couch in Columbus.
segments.tr: यह रविवार है, रात 9 बजे, और आप कोलंबस में सोफे पर हैं।

segments.src: You land on QVC.
segments.tr: आप QVC पर उतरते हैं।

segments.src: A host is demonstrating a countertop grill — flipping it open, pressing a sandwich, talking about the removable plates.
segments.tr: एक मेजबान एक काउंटरटॉप ग्रिल का प्रदर्शन कर रहा है — इसे खोल रहा है, एक सैंडविच दबा रहा है, हटाने योग्य प्लेटों के बारे में बात कर रहा है।

segments.src: A counter on screen says how many have sold, and the price is only good for this segment.
segments.tr: स्क्रीन पर एक काउंटर कहता है कि कितने बेचे गए हैं, और कीमत केवल इस सेगमेंट के लिए अच्छी है।

segments.src: You weren't shopping for a grill.
segments.tr: आप ग्रिल के लिए खरीद रहे नहीं थे।

segments.src: That's the point: **seller-controlled time, demonstration, urgency.** Home shopping has thrived for decades on categories that are hard to judge from a photo but easy to *show* — kitchen gadgets, jewelry, skincare, mattresses.
segments.tr: यह बिंदु है: **विक्रेता-नियंत्रित समय, प्रदर्शन, तात्कालिकता।** होम शॉपिंग दशकों से उन श्रेणियों पर पनपा है जो फोटो से आंकना मुश्किल है लेकिन *दिखाने* में आसान है — रसोई गैजेट, गहने, स्किनकेयर, गद्दे।

segments.src: You pick up your phone instead and search Amazon for "panini press."
segments.tr: आप इसके बजाय अपना फोन उठाते हैं और Amazon पर "panini press" के लिए खोज करते हैं।

segments.src: Forty results, sorted by review count.
segments.tr: चालीस परिणाम, समीक्षा गणना द्वारा क्रमबद्ध।

segments.src: You read three one-star reviews, check that it's Prime, and see it arrives Tuesday.
segments.tr: आप तीन एक-सितारा समीक्षाएं पढ़ते हैं, यह जांचते हैं कि यह Prime है, और यह देखते हैं कि यह मंगलवार को आता है।

segments.src: **Shopper-controlled time.** Nobody persuaded you of anything; you compared and picked.
segments.tr: **खरीदार-नियंत्रित समय।** किसी ने आपको कुछ भी राजी नहीं किया; आपने तुलना की और चुना।

segments.src: Then you open Instagram and a video shows leggings for $34.
segments.tr: फिर आप Instagram खोलते हैं और एक वीडियो $34 के लिए लेगिंग दिखाता है।

segments.src: Two taps, Apple Pay, done, before the video finishes.
segments.tr: दो टैप, Apple Pay, हो गया, वीडियो खत्म होने से पहले।

segments.src: You never visited a website.
segments.tr: आप कभी किसी वेबसाइट पर नहीं गए।

segments.src: In the U.S., most e-commerce traffic now comes through a phone, and checkout friction — not price — is often what decides the sale.
segments.tr: U.S. में, अधिकांश ई-कॉमर्स ट्रैफिक अब एक फोन के माध्यम से आता है, और चेकआउट घर्षण — कीमत नहीं — अक्सर वह है जो बिक्री का फैसला करता है।

segments.src: Three retail formats, one couch, twenty minutes.
segments.tr: तीन खुदरा प्रारूप, एक सोफा, बीस मिनट।

segments.src: Now the economics.
segments.tr: अब अर्थशास्त्र।

segments.src: The leggings don't fit.
segments.tr: लेगिंग फिट नहीं होती।

segments.src: You get a free return label, drop the bag at the UPS counter inside a Kohl's, and forget about it.
segments.tr: आप एक मुफ्त रिटर्न लेबल प्राप्त करते हैं, Kohl's के अंदर UPS काउंटर पर बैग ड्रॉप करते हैं, और इसे भूल जाते हैं।

segments.src: For you it cost nothing.
segments.tr: आपके लिए इसकी कोई कीमत नहीं है।

segments.src: For the seller: outbound shipping, return shipping, someone inspecting the bag, and possibly reselling at a discount.
segments.tr: विक्रेता के लिए: आउटबाउंड शिपिंग, रिटर्न शिपिंग, कोई बैग का निरीक्षण, और संभवतः छूट पर पुनः विक्रय।

segments.src: That single return can erase the margin on the sale — which is exactly why "free returns" is quietly disappearing at a lot of retailers, and why buy-online-pickup-in-store exists.
segments.tr: वह एकल रिटर्न बिक्री पर मार्जिन को मिटा सकता है — जो बिल्कुल यही कारण है कि "मुफ्त रिटर्न" बहुत सारे खुदरा विक्रेताओं में चुप्पी से गायब हो रहा है, और क्यों खरीद-ऑनलाइन-पिकअप-इन-स्टोर मौजूद है।

segments.src: BOPIS lets the store's building do the last mile for free.
segments.tr: BOPIS स्टोर की इमारत को अंतिम मील को मुफ्त में करने देता है।

segments.src: And a number worth keeping in your head: e-commerce is roughly **one in six** U.S.
segments.tr: और आपके सिर में रखने के लायक एक संख्या: ई-कॉमर्स लगभग **छह में से एक** U.S.

segments.src: retail dollars, per Census Bureau estimates.
segments.tr: खुदरा डॉलर, Census Bureau अनुमान के अनुसार।

segments.src: Enormous — and also a reminder that about five in six are still spent in a building.
segments.tr: विशाल — और यह भी एक अनुस्मारक है कि लगभग छह में से पाँच अभी भी एक इमारत में खर्च किए जाते हैं।

segments.src: Non-store retailing didn't replace stores.
segments.tr: गैर-दुकान खुदरा ने दुकानों को प्रतिस्थापित नहीं किया।

segments.src: It stripped them of their monopoly on selection, hours, and geography, and forced them to compete on the things a warehouse can't do.
segments.tr: इसने चयन, घंटे, और भूगोल पर अपने एकाधिकार को छीन लिया, और उन्हें उन चीजों पर प्रतिस्पर्धा करने के लिए मजबूर किया जो एक गोदाम नहीं कर सकता।

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-लाइन रीकैप

segments.src: 1. Non-store retailing sells without a sales floor — TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce are its dominant modern forms.
segments.tr: 1. गैर-दुकान खुदरा एक बिक्री फर्श के बिना बेचता है — टीवी होम शॉपिंग, ऑनलाइन मार्केटप्लेस, और मोबाइल वाणिज्य इसके प्रभावशाली आधुनिक रूप हैं।

segments.src: 2. It escapes rent, shelf limits, store hours, and trade-area boundaries, but pays for it in customer acquisition, last-mile delivery, and returns.
segments.tr: 2. यह किराया, शेल्फ सीमा, दुकान घंटे, और व्यापार-क्षेत्र सीमा से बचता है, लेकिन ग्राहक अधिग्रहण, अंतिम-मील डिलीवरी, और रिटर्न में इसके लिए भुगतान करता है।

segments.src: 3. The formats differ by *who controls the clock*: home shopping and social feeds create demand; search-driven marketplaces capture demand that already exists.
segments.tr: 3. प्रारूप *जो घड़ी को नियंत्रित करता है* से भिन्न हैं: होम शॉपिंग और सामाजिक फ़ीड मांग बनाते हैं; खोज-संचालित मार्केटप्लेस पहले से मौजूद मांग को कैप्चर करते हैं।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: **1.** Which cost is generally *higher* for a pure online retailer than for a comparable physical store?
segments.tr: **1.** एक शुद्ध ऑनलाइन खुदरा विक्रेता के लिए कौन सी लागत आम तौर पर एक तुलनीय भौतिक दुकान की तुलना में *अधिक* है?

segments.src: - (a) Rent per square foot
segments.tr: - (a) प्रति वर्ग फुट किराया

segments.src: - (b) In-store labor
segments.tr: - (b) इन-स्टोर श्रम

segments.src: - (c) Reverse logistics (handling returns)
segments.tr: - (c) रिवर्स लॉजिस्टिक्स (रिटर्न संभालना)

segments.src: - (d) Shrinkage from shoplifting
segments.tr: - (d) दुकान चोरी से संकुचन

segments.src: **2.** TV home shopping and live-stream commerce share the same core mechanic: the seller controls when the product is shown and creates urgency around it.
segments.tr: **2.** टीवी होम शॉपिंग और लाइव-स्ट्रीम वाणिज्य एक ही मूल यांत्रिकी साझा करते हैं: विक्रेता नियंत्रित करता है कि उत्पाद कब दिखाया जाता है और इसके चारों ओर तात्कालिकता बनाता है।

segments.src: **3.** "Endless aisle" refers to:
segments.tr: **3.** "अंतहीन गलियारा" संदर्भित करता है:

segments.src: - (a) A warehouse club's long shelving runs
segments.tr: - (a) एक गोदाम क्लब की लंबी शेलिंग चलता है

segments.src: - (b) An online retailer's ability to list far more SKUs than a store can stock
segments.tr: - (b) एक ऑनलाइन खुदरा विक्रेता की क्षमता एक दुकान स्टॉक कर सकते हैं की तुलना में कई अधिक SKU सूचीबद्ध करने के लिए

segments.src: - (c) A store layout that forces shoppers past every category
segments.tr: - (c) एक दुकान लेआउट जो खरीदार को हर श्रेणी के पास मजबूर करता है

segments.src: - (d) A 24-hour store format
segments.tr: - (d) एक 24 घंटे की दुकान प्रारूप

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Non-store retailing** — selling to final consumers without a fixed physical sales floor: direct selling, vending, catalogs, TV home shopping, e-commerce, and m-commerce.
segments.tr: - **गैर-दुकान खुदरा** — एक निश्चित भौतिक बिक्री फर्श के बिना अंतिम उपभोक्ताओं को बेचना: प्रत्यक्ष विक्रय, वेंडिंग, कैटलॉग, टीवी होम शॉपिंग, ई-कॉमर्स, और एम-कॉमर्स।

segments.src: - **Endless aisle** — the ability to offer a near-unlimited assortment because listings cost data storage rather than shelf space.

es.title: [Retailing 101 #6] El Pasillo en tu Bolsillo: Retail sin Tienda

segments.src: > Non-store retailing doesn't delete the costs of a store — it trades rent and shelf space for shipping, returns, and the price of getting your attention.
segments.tr: > El retail sin tienda no elimina los costos de una tienda — intercambia renta y espacio de estantes por envíos, devoluciones y el precio de obtener tu atención.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Every lecture so far has assumed a building: a sales floor, a door, a trade area of people who live close enough to walk in.
segments.tr: Toda conferencia hasta ahora ha asumido un edificio: un piso de ventas, una puerta, un área de mercado de personas que viven lo suficientemente cerca para entrar.

segments.src: **Non-store retailing** is everything that sells to final consumers without that floor — direct selling (the Mary Kay rep), automated vending (the machine in the hotel lobby), catalogs and direct mail, TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce.
segments.tr: **El retail sin tienda** es todo lo que vende a consumidores finales sin ese piso — venta directa (el representante de Mary Kay), máquinas expendedoras automatizadas (la máquina en el vestíbulo del hotel), catálogos y correo directo, compra por TV en casa, mercados en línea y comercio móvil.

segments.src: The three that matter most today are the last three.
segments.tr: Los tres que más importan hoy son los últimos tres.

segments.src: Here's the useful way to think about them.
segments.tr: Aquí está la forma útil de pensar en ellos.

segments.src: A physical store operates under three hard limits:
segments.tr: Una tienda física opera bajo tres límites difíciles:

segments.src: 1. **Shelf space** — a Target carries maybe 80,000 items because that's what fits.
segments.tr: 1. **Espacio de estantes** — una Target lleva quizás 80.000 artículos porque es lo que cabe.

segments.src: 2. **Store hours** — closed at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 2. **Horario de la tienda** — cerrada a las 11 p.m.

segments.src: 3. **Trade area** — it sells to whoever is within a reasonable drive.
segments.tr: 3. **Área de mercado** — vende a quien esté dentro de un viaje razonable.

segments.src: Non-store formats break all three.
segments.tr: Los formatos sin tienda rompen los tres.

segments.src: An online marketplace has an *endless aisle*: adding the 400,000th product costs a database row, not a square foot.
segments.tr: Un mercado en línea tiene un *pasillo sin fin*: agregar el producto número 400.000 cuesta una fila de base de datos, no un pie cuadrado.

segments.src: It's open at 2 a.m.
segments.tr: Está abierto a las 2 a.m.

segments.src: Its trade area is the shipping map.
segments.tr: Su área de mercado es el mapa de envío.

segments.src: But — and this is the part beginners miss — **you don't escape cost, you swap it.** A store's big costs are rent, store labor, and inventory sitting on shelves.
segments.tr: Pero — y esta es la parte que los principiantes pierden — **no escapas del costo, lo intercambias.** Los grandes costos de una tienda son renta, mano de obra de tienda e inventario en estantes.

segments.src: A non-store retailer pays little rent, and instead pays for:
segments.tr: Un minorista sin tienda paga poca renta y, en su lugar, paga por:

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition** — a store on a busy corner gets foot traffic for free. An online seller buys every visitor through ads, search placement, or a marketplace commission.
segments.tr: - **Adquisición de clientes** — una tienda en una esquina ocupada obtiene tráfico peatonal gratis. Un vendedor en línea compra cada visitante a través de anuncios, posicionamiento en búsqueda o una comisión del mercado.

segments.src: - **Fulfillment and the last mile** — picking, packing, and driving one box to one doorstep. A store makes the *customer* do that leg for free.
segments.tr: - **Fulfillment y la última milla** — recoger, empacar y llevar una caja a una puerta. Una tienda hace que el *cliente* haga ese tramo gratis.

segments.src: - **Returns (reverse logistics)** — a shopper who can't touch the product buys two sizes and sends one back. Online return rates run well above in-store rates, and apparel is the worst offender. Each return means shipping paid twice, inspection, repackaging, and often a markdown.
segments.tr: - **Devoluciones (logística inversa)** — un comprador que no puede tocar el producto compra dos tamaños y devuelve uno. Las tasas de devolución en línea son mucho más altas que las tasas en tienda, y la ropa es el peor infractor. Cada devolución significa envío pagado dos veces, inspección, reempaquetado y a menudo una rebaja.

segments.src: And because the shopper can't touch anything, the retailer must supply **trust substitutes**: photos and video, ratings and reviews, size charts, a generous return policy, a recognizable brand.
segments.tr: Y porque el comprador no puede tocar nada, el minorista debe proporcionar **sustitutos de confianza**: fotos y video, calificaciones y reseñas, tablas de tamaño, una política de devolución generosa, una marca reconocible.

segments.src: That's not marketing decoration.
segments.tr: Eso no es decoración de marketing.

segments.src: It's doing the job the shelf used to do.
segments.tr: Está haciendo el trabajo que el estante solía hacer.

segments.src: One more distinction worth carrying around — **who controls the clock**:
segments.tr: Una distinción más que vale la pena llevar — **quién controla el reloj**:

segments.src: - **TV home shopping** — the *seller* controls it. A scheduled hour, a host demonstrating, a countdown, "only 300 left." You didn't go looking; the format created the demand.
segments.tr: - **Compra por TV en casa** — el *vendedor* la controla. Una hora programada, un anfitrión demostrando, una cuenta regresiva, "solo 300 quedan". No fuiste a buscar; el formato creó la demanda.

segments.src: - **Online marketplace** — the *shopper* controls it. You search, filter, compare, and buy on your own schedule. Demand already existed; the retailer competes on price, selection, and delivery speed.
segments.tr: - **Mercado en línea** — el *comprador* lo controla. Buscas, filtras, comparas y compras en tu propio horario. La demanda ya existía; el minorista compite en precio, selección y velocidad de entrega.

segments.src: - **Mobile / social commerce** — back to the seller. A feed pushes you something you weren't shopping for, and checkout takes fifteen seconds because your card is already saved.
segments.tr: - **Comercio móvil / social** — de vuelta al vendedor. Un feed te empuja algo que no estabas comprando, y el pago toma quince segundos porque tu tarjeta ya está guardada.

segments.src: Which is why **live commerce** — a host demonstrating a product in a live stream with a countdown — isn't new at all.
segments.tr: Por eso **comercio en vivo** — un anfitrión demostrando un producto en una transmisión en vivo con una cuenta regresiva — no es nada nuevo.

segments.src: It's TV home shopping, rebuilt on a phone, with a comment section.
segments.tr: Es compra por TV en casa, reconstruida en un teléfono, con una sección de comentarios.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: It's Sunday, 9 p.m., and you're on the couch in Columbus.
segments.tr: Es domingo, 9 p.m., y estás en el sofá en Columbus.

segments.src: You land on QVC.
segments.tr: Llegas a QVC.

segments.src: A host is demonstrating a countertop grill — flipping it open, pressing a sandwich, talking about the removable plates.
segments.tr: Un anfitrión está demostrando una parrilla de mostrador — abriendo, presionando un sándwich, hablando sobre las placas desmontables.

segments.src: A counter on screen says how many have sold, and the price is only good for this segment.
segments.tr: Un contador en pantalla dice cuántos se han vendido, y el precio solo es válido para este segmento.

segments.src: You weren't shopping for a grill.
segments.tr: No estabas comprando una parrilla.

segments.src: That's the point: **seller-controlled time, demonstration, urgency.** Home shopping has thrived for decades on categories that are hard to judge from a photo but easy to *show* — kitchen gadgets, jewelry, skincare, mattresses.
segments.tr: Ese es el punto: **tiempo controlado por el vendedor, demostración, urgencia.** La compra en casa ha prosperado durante décadas en categorías que son difíciles de juzgar por una foto pero fáciles de *mostrar* — gadgets de cocina, joyas, cuidado de la piel, colchones.

segments.src: You pick up your phone instead and search Amazon for "panini press."
segments.tr: En su lugar, tomas tu teléfono y buscas en Amazon "panini press".

segments.src: Forty results, sorted by review count.
segments.tr: Cuarenta resultados, ordenados por número de reseñas.

segments.src: You read three one-star reviews, check that it's Prime, and see it arrives Tuesday.
segments.tr: Lees tres reseñas de una estrella, verificas que es Prime y ves que llega el martes.

segments.src: **Shopper-controlled time.** Nobody persuaded you of anything; you compared and picked.
segments.tr: **Tiempo controlado por el comprador.** Nadie te persuadió de nada; comparaste y elegiste.

segments.src: Then you open Instagram and a video shows leggings for $34.
segments.tr: Luego abres Instagram y un video muestra mallas por $34.

segments.src: Two taps, Apple Pay, done, before the video finishes.
segments.tr: Dos toques, Apple Pay, listo, antes de que el video termine.

segments.src: You never visited a website.
segments.tr: Nunca visitaste un sitio web.

segments.src: In the U.S., most e-commerce traffic now comes through a phone, and checkout friction — not price — is often what decides the sale.
segments.tr: En los EE.UU., la mayoría del tráfico de comercio electrónico ahora proviene de un teléfono, y la fricción de pago — no el precio — es a menudo lo que decide la venta.

segments.src: Three retail formats, one couch, twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Tres formatos minoristas, un sofá, veinte minutos.

segments.src: Now the economics.
segments.tr: Ahora la economía.

segments.src: The leggings don't fit.
segments.tr: Las mallas no caben.

segments.src: You get a free return label, drop the bag at the UPS counter inside a Kohl's, and forget about it.
segments.tr: Obtienes una etiqueta de devolución gratuita, dejas la bolsa en el mostrador de UPS dentro de una Kohl's y lo olvidas.

segments.src: For you it cost nothing.
segments.tr: Para ti no costó nada.

segments.src: For the seller: outbound shipping, return shipping, someone inspecting the bag, and possibly reselling at a discount.
segments.tr: Para el vendedor: envío de salida, envío de devolución, alguien inspeccionando la bolsa y posiblemente revendiendo con descuento.

segments.src: That single return can erase the margin on the sale — which is exactly why "free returns" is quietly disappearing at a lot of retailers, and why buy-online-pickup-in-store exists.
segments.tr: Esa sola devolución puede borrar el margen en la venta — que es exactamente por qué las "devoluciones gratuitas" desaparecen silenciosamente en muchos minoristas y por qué existe comprar en línea y recoger en tienda.

segments.src: BOPIS lets the store's building do the last mile for free.
segments.tr: BOPIS permite que el edificio de la tienda haga la última milla gratis.

segments.src: And a number worth keeping in your head: e-commerce is roughly **one in six** U.S.
segments.tr: Y un número que vale la pena recordar: el comercio electrónico es aproximadamente **uno de cada seis** EE.UU.

segments.src: retail dollars, per Census Bureau estimates.
segments.tr: dólares minoristas, según las estimaciones de la Oficina del Censo.

segments.src: Enormous — and also a reminder that about five in six are still spent in a building.
segments.tr: Enorme — y también un recordatorio de que aproximadamente cinco de cada seis todavía se gastan en un edificio.

segments.src: Non-store retailing didn't replace stores.
segments.tr: El retail sin tienda no reemplazó las tiendas.

segments.src: It stripped them of their monopoly on selection, hours, and geography, and forced them to compete on the things a warehouse can't do.
segments.tr: Los despojó de su monopolio sobre la selección, horarios y geografía, y los obligó a competir en cosas que un almacén no puede hacer.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## El Resumen de 3 Líneas

segments.src: 1. Non-store retailing sells without a sales floor — TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce are its dominant modern forms.
segments.tr: 1. El retail sin tienda vende sin un piso de ventas — la compra por TV en casa, los mercados en línea y el comercio móvil son sus formas modernas dominantes.

segments.src: 2. It escapes rent, shelf limits, store hours, and trade-area boundaries, but pays for it in customer acquisition, last-mile delivery, and returns.
segments.tr: 2. Escapa de la renta, límites de estantes, horarios de tienda y límites del área de mercado, pero lo paga en adquisición de clientes, entrega de última milla y devoluciones.

segments.src: 3. The formats differ by *who controls the clock*: home shopping and social feeds create demand; search-driven marketplaces capture demand that already exists.
segments.tr: 3. Los formatos difieren por *quién controla el reloj*: la compra en casa y los feeds sociales crean demanda; los mercados impulsados por búsqueda capturan la demanda que ya existe.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** Which cost is generally *higher* for a pure online retailer than for a comparable physical store?
segments.tr: **1.** ¿Qué costo es generalmente *más alto* para un minorista en línea puro que para una tienda física comparable?

segments.src: - (a) Rent per square foot
segments.tr: - (a) Renta por pie cuadrado

segments.src: - (b) In-store labor
segments.tr: - (b) Mano de obra en tienda

segments.src: - (c) Reverse logistics (handling returns)
segments.tr: - (c) Logística inversa (manejo de devoluciones)

segments.src: - (d) Shrinkage from shoplifting
segments.tr: - (d) Merma por robo

segments.src: **2.** TV home shopping and live-stream commerce share the same core mechanic: the seller controls when the product is shown and creates urgency around it.
segments.tr: **2.** La compra por TV en casa y el comercio de transmisión en vivo comparten la misma mecánica central: el vendedor controla cuándo se muestra el producto y crea urgencia en torno a él.

segments.src: **3.** "Endless aisle" refers to:
segments.tr: **3.** "Pasillo sin fin" se refiere a:

segments.src: - (a) A warehouse club's long shelving runs
segments.tr: - (a) Las largas corridas de estantería de un club de almacén

segments.src: - (b) An online retailer's ability to list far more SKUs than a store can stock
segments.tr: - (b) La capacidad de un minorista en línea de listar muchos más SKUs de lo que una tienda puede almacenar

segments.src: - (c) A store layout that forces shoppers past every category
segments.tr: - (c) Un diseño de tienda que obliga a los compradores a pasar por cada categoría

segments.src: - (d) A 24-hour store format
segments.tr: - (d) Un formato de tienda de 24 horas

segments.tr: ## 📚 Los Términos de Hoy

segments.tr: - **Retail sin tienda** — venta a consumidores finales sin un piso de ventas físico fijo: venta directa, máquinas expendedoras, catálogos, compra por TV en casa, comercio electrónico y comercio móvil.

segments.src: - **Endless aisle** — the ability to offer a near-unlimited assortment because listings cost data storage rather than shelf space.
segments.tr: - **Pasillo sin fin** — la capacidad de ofrecer un surtido casi ilimitado porque los listados cuestan almacenamiento de datos en lugar de espacio de estantes.

segments.src: - **Customer acquisition cost (CAC)** — what a retailer pays in ads, commissions, or promotions to bring in one buying customer; the online substitute for a good street corner.
segments.tr: - **Costo de adquisición de clientes (CAC)** — lo que un minorista paga en anuncios, comisiones o promociones para traer un cliente comprador; el sustituto en línea para una buena esquina.

segments.src: - **Last mile** — the final delivery leg from local facility to the customer's door; the most expensive stretch of the supply chain, and the one stores hand to the shopper for free.
segments.tr: - **Última milla** — el tramo final de entrega desde la instalación local hasta la puerta del cliente; el tramo más caro de la cadena de suministro, y el que las tiendas entregan al comprador gratis.

segments.src: - **Reverse logistics** — the process and cost of moving returned goods back, inspecting, restocking, or disposing of them.
segments.tr: - **Logística inversa** — el proceso y costo de mover las mercancías devueltas, inspeccionarlas, reabastecer o desecharlas.

segments.src: - **Live commerce** — real-time video selling with in-stream checkout; structurally, TV home shopping rebuilt for mobile.
segments.tr: - **Comercio en vivo** — venta de video en tiempo real con pago en transmisión; estructuralmente, compra por TV en casa reconstruida para móvil.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## المفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Every lecture so far has assumed a building: a sales floor, a door, a trade area of people who live close enough to walk in.
segments.tr: كل محاضرة حتى الآن افترضت وجود مبنى: منطقة بيع، باب، منطقة تجارية من الأشخاص الذين يعيشون قريباً بما يكفي للدخول.

segments.src: **Non-store retailing** is everything that sells to final consumers without that floor — direct selling (the Mary Kay rep), automated vending (the machine in the hotel lobby), catalogs and direct mail, TV home shopping, online marketplaces, and mobile commerce.
